evidence.note: Designed a fallback DB-poll loop alongside the broadcast broker up front, anticipating broker loss — resilience was designed-in, so later the agent had a design to fall back on rather than needing a reactive re-architecture.

Long broker-death debugging loop: repeatedly probed POST/login/fan-out after killing the broker under many permutations (supervisor stopped/resumed, executor, curl, verbose). Much of this is local retrying of the same check, showing circling before root cause was found.

Escaped the loop by restarting cleanly and discovering the kill wasn't hitting the real broker PID ('Find broker pid (real)' → 'Real broker-kill test by PID'); recognized the failing signal was largely a test-harness artifact and corrected methodology instead of pointlessly re-architecting the design.

Re-verified across the failure matrix with corrected tests: killed an HTTP node and awaited respawn, and re-ran broker-SIGKILL fan-out tests with fixed selectors/payload keys — confirming fixes rather than assuming.
On Playwright UI failures, read app.js, grepped testids, and made several targeted edits with re-runs — competent local fix-and-verify, but symptom-level rather than design revision.

reasoning: The agent consistently diagnoses failures and re-verifies after fixes, and notably escaped a circular broker-death debugging stretch by isolating the root cause (a mis-targeted kill / test-harness artifact) and correcting its verification methodology — behavior above anchor 5. However, the core resilience design (DB-poll fallback) was built anticipatorily rather than re-architected in response to a genuinely falsified invariant, and the middle of the trajectory shows real circling before the breakthrough, so it falls short of anchor 8's targeted design change on a broken core assumption. Level 6 interpolates between these.
